To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteomic analysis of NM in PHN, a model for early stage of liver carcinogenesis, showed that the NM is a dynamic structure and that the changes in NM morphology and protein composition are synchronous with changes in the ability of these proteins to bind nuclear DNA and RNA.
we have identified 23 differentially expressed proteins in the NM of PHN in respect to the normal NM.
the nuclear matrix in PHN is characterized by the deregulated expression and altered binding to MARs of several proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the role played by the NM in carcinogenesis.
the proteomic analysis of the NM in PHN and the detection of differentially expressed NM proteins.
the identification of differentially regulated proteins and MAR-binding proteins in PHN, and the results provide new insight into the role of these proteins in the carcinogenesis process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NM is involved in the process of hepatocarcinogenesis and the changes in the protein expression profile are synchronous with changes in the ability of the NM proteins to bind MARs.
the changes observed in the NM of PHN are related to the altered expression of specific NM proteins that are involved in the maintenance of chromatin structure.

, in PHN, the expression of NM proteins is altered and that the changes observed in the NM morphology are related to the changes in the expression of these proteins, which in turn are responsible for the changes in NM functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in PHN there is a decrease in basic proteins that bind to nuclear RNA and an increase in proteins that bind MARs, which may contribute to chromatin reorganization and tumor progression.
the proteome of the NM undergoes significant changes in PHN, which are related to the altered morphology of the NM.
the changes in the protein profile of NM are related to both the changes in the structure of NM and the changes in the ability of NM to bind MARs sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the changes in the protein content of the NM, in particular the expression of MAR-binding proteins, are closely related to the morphological changes observed in the NM of PHN.
the proteome of the nuclear matrix is a dynamic system that is able to respond to the changes occurring in the nuclear structure and function.
the proteome of the NM is altered in PHN and this alteration is synchronous with changes in both the morphology of the NM and its ability to bind nuclear RNA or DNA containing MAR sequences.
